subject.title: [Feature]: WebUI notification system, cron job management popups, and context monitor integration

question: Should OpenClaw define a shared connected-Control-UI notification/action queue for cron results and context pressure, and should cron snooze/reschedule mutate existing jobs or create one-shot follow-ups?
rationale: The missing behavior is real, but the durable boundary affects UI architecture, cron scheduling semantics, context UX, Web Push/admin-notify overlap, and Webchat action work.

options.title: Design Shared UI Notifications First
options.body: Add a single Control UI notification/action contract and then implement cron-result and context-pressure actions on top of it.

options.title: Fold Into Webchat Actions
options.body: Treat this as part of the broader Webchat inline-button/callback contract so chat, cron, and notification actions share one callback path.

options.title: Defer In-App Popups
options.body: Keep current support to inline context warnings, cron history, and Web Push settings until a larger notification roadmap is chosen.

recommendation.title: Design Shared UI Notifications First
recommendation.body: Add a single Control UI notification/action contract and then implement cron-result and context-pressure actions on top of it.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision crosses cron gateway behavior, notification delivery, and product UX boundaries where steipete has the strongest recent history signal.
